statement: A compensation execution is distinct from its originating execution.
Failure of an originating execution does not imply authority for a compensation execution.
A compensation execution cannot cross its consequential boundary without independent current authority and admission.
Successful compensation does not erase historical occurrence of the originating execution.
Economic equivalence after compensation does not imply historical-state identity.
A compensation event that itself partially effects state requires any later repair to be independently instantiated and admitted.
